items.problem: No test goes through the login session discard of `purchase` (`open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:160`) at its three places before `finish`. Removing the epoch check at line 412 (`buy` runs with the account token of the previous session), removing the check at line 443 (`VerifyPurchase` goes out in the new session), or removing it at line 451 (`finish` is called and the result is not discarded) each leaves all 74 PaymentCore tests passing. `test_login_session_change_during_finish_rejects_the_purchase` in `tests/test_purchase.gd:92` changes the session only after the verify response. This existed before the range.

No test covers a login session that changes during `list_unfinished` or `list_owned`. Removing this check leaves all 74 PaymentCore tests passing, and each listed transaction then sends `RecoverPurchase` with the receipt in the new session before line 679 discards the response. `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:160` discards the operation at that point. `tests/test_recovery.gd:155` changes the session only after `RecoverPurchase` was sent. This existed before the range.

`SessionEndedEvent` as a login session change (`open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:146` and `:159`) has no test. No PaymentCore test ends a session: every session change in `tests/` is `log_in`. Making `_on_login_session_changed` return when `AuthCore.is_logged_in` is `false`, which ignores this event, leaves all 74 tests passing, so the `finish` success list and the store `GOOGLE` restore flag could survive the end of a session. This existed before the range.

"When a `recover_purchases` is in progress, returns that one's result" (`open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:144`) has no test. Removing lines 525 to 529 leaves all 74 tests passing, although a second call then runs `list_unfinished` again and returns its own `RecoverySummary`. `test_two_prepares_at_once_connect_once_and_share_the_result` and `test_google_restore_of_paymentcore_is_shared_with_a_content_restore` cover the same rule for `prepare` and `restore_purchases` only. This existed before the range.

"`0` when `TimeCore.is_synced` is `false`" of `get_pass_days_left` (`open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:168`) has no test. No PaymentCore test reads a pass before the first time sync. Removing `or not TimeCore.is_synced()` here leaves all 74 tests passing, although `_today()` then computes from `get_current_day` returning 0, so a held pass reports a wrong positive number of days left and `is_owned` and `can_claim_daily` follow it. This existed before the range.

Two defining documents set a different log level. This line says that the `RecoverPurchase` failure callback returns `true` for every failure with "warn log, no screen". `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/network-core.md:106` and `:264` make only a `ServerError` warn and give a communication failure one error log even when the callback returns `true`, and `client/godot/core/network_core/network_core.gd:1154` does that. Run path: on a foreground return with no network, each unfinished transaction writes an error log, not the warn this line states. The PaymentCore tests check only `IAP_VERIFY_UNAVAILABLE`, so they do not show the difference. This existed before the range.

`claim_daily` has no login session check, so it returns `true` for a claim whose login session ended. This differs from `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:160`, which ends an async operation of an ended session with the failure value (`false` in the API table at line 41). Reproduced with a test in a temporary copy: `add_pending(core/ClaimIapDaily)`, `claim_daily` of `[iap_vip]`, `log_in` of another user, then `release_pending` with a success response. `claim_daily` returned `true`. This existed before the range.

`_run_purchase` does not check the login session after `buy` returns before it returns `Cancelled` (line 435), `Pending` (line 437) or `StoreFailed` (line 440); its first check after `buy` is at line 443, on the `Success` path. `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:160` requires the failure value, `Rejected`. Reproduced with a test in a temporary copy using an adapter whose `buy` waits: `purchase` of `[iap_gems]`, `log_in` of another user during `buy`, then `buy` ends. With `Cancelled` the result was `Cancelled`, and with `Pending` it was `Pending`, not `Rejected`. The `StoreFailed` path was read in the code and not run. This existed before the range.

For store `GOOGLE`, the restore of a new login session joins a `restore_purchases` still running from the previous session, and line 546 has already set `_google_restored` to `true`. The joined result is discarded and `list_owned` does not run again in that session, although `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/payment-core.md:146` has one restore per login session. Reproduced with a test in a temporary copy: first `recover_purchases` of session A, its restore held on `RecoverPurchase`, `log_in` of another user, `recover_purchases` in the new session, the held response released, then `recover_purchases` again. `list_owned` stayed at 1 call and `_google_restored` was `true`. The same join makes a `restore_purchases` that content code calls in the new session wait for the old session's run; that path was read in the code and not run. This existed before the range.
